title: Guidelines regarding company names
text:
LINCOLN CONSULTANCY (MYANMAR) LIMITED
CONVENIENCE TRANSLATION - ACCURACY NOT GUARANTEED
Guidelines regarding company names
The Directorate of Investment and Company Administration (DICA) is reviewing and permitting company
names according to the provisions in sections 25 to 27 Myanmar Companies Law (2017). However, in
practice, business owners are facing unnecessary delays in the registration process because the chosen
company name is not in compliance with the law or fails to meet requirements. Although some company
names are not directly prohibited by law, they are names that may only be permitted with restrictions
depending on the situation, or names that require detailed scrutiny based on policy. To increase
transparency in the company registration process and to reduce the time spent by business owners
(efficiency), the registrars/officers who scrutinise company names among others verify the following:
1. Identical or similar names
Company names submitted for registration that are similar to existing names and are likely to
mislead the public are mainly restricted as follows:
(a) A name that is completely identical or extremely similar to the name of an existing
company is not permitted. (Examples: K.M.L Co., Ltd and KML Co., Ltd. and K-M-L Co.,
Ltd.; or Global 1 Co., Ltd. and Global One Co., Ltd.; or GlObal Co., Ltd. and Global Co., Ltd.;
or Gold Co., Ltd. and Shwe Co., Ltd.; or Su Latt Co., Ltd. and Hsu Lat Co., Ltd.)
(b) Applying to use the name of an existing company by adding words such as "Group",
"Holding", "International", "Myanmar", "Family" after it is not permitted.
(c) Names that are not identical to those of existing companies but have a similar
pronunciation or only slight differences in spelling are not permitted. (Example:
Ayeyarwady Trading Co., Ltd and Irrawaddy Trading Co., Ltd.)
(d) Applying for a name that rearranges the order of words in an existing company's name is
not permitted. (Example: Mandalay City Trading Co., Ltd and City Mandalay Trading Co.,
Ltd)
(e) Names that, although slightly different in spelling, seem similar are not permitted.
(Example: "Khaing" and "Khine")
(f) It is not permitted to apply for names in which two country names are joined, which might
cause the public to mistakenly believe that there is a government-to-government
connection, to confuse the company with business associations, or to mistakenly believe
that there are bilateral agreements. (Examples: Myanmar Thai, or Myanmar China)

(h) It is not permitted to create a new company name by combining the brand name of an
existing company with an abbreviation for the brand name or for the business type.
(Example: Zay Ya Co., Ltd. and Zay Ya (ZY) Co., Ltd.; or Zay Ya Technology Co., Ltd. and Zay
Ya Tech Co., Ltd.; or Zay Ya Travels & Tours Co., Ltd. and Zay Ya T & T Co., Ltd.)
2. Prohibited or restricted words
(a) Affiliation with the government
Names may not be used without permission if they contain expressions that falsely
suggest a direct affiliation with the State, such as “State Government”, “State”, “Central
Bank”, “Union Government”, “President”, “Ministry”, or “Government of Myanmar”, or
“Ministry of Myanmar”, “Department”, “[Government] Office”, or any other expression
proposed or endorsed by any organisation.
(b) In addition to the expressions above, certain other expressions, although not specified in
the law, are restricted as follows:
(1) International organisations
Names that suggest an affiliation with international organisations such as the UN,
WHO, ASEAN.
(2) Names that are culturally and religiously sensitive
Avoid using vulgar expressions or inappropriate language.
Names that may cause religious or ethnic conflict, or cause controversy.
(3) Political terms
(4) Names that the Registrar directs not use depending on circumstances and time.
3. Regarding the name of any existing company, the Registrar may, even if he has already permitted
registration of the company according to the provisions of the Myanmar Companies Law (2017),
direct to change the name according to section 26 if he deems the name not to be in compliance
with the law or to be an inappropriate name for registration.

title: Regulations on Licencing Foreign Remittance Businesses
text:

Republic of the Union of Myanmar
Central Bank of Myanmar
Notification No. 18/2026

Exercising the powers conferred by section 49 (a) Foreign Exchange Management Law, the Central Bank
of Myanmar hereby issues the following Regulations with the consent of the Union Government.
Chapter 1
Title, application and definitions
1. These Regulations may be cited as the Regulations on Licencing Foreign Remittance Businesses.
2. These Regulations shall apply to companies established in Myanmar and to remittance business
licence holders that wish to operate a foreign remittance business.
3. Expressions in these Regulations shall have the meanings as defined in the Foreign Exchange
Management Law. Furthermore, the following expressions shall have the meanings given
hereunder:
(a) “Remittance business” means accepting money for a remittance and sending it from
Myanmar to a foreign country, or receiving a remittance made by another remittance
business abroad or one’s own agent or branch office abroad and paying out the money in
Myanmar.
(b) “Remittance business licence” means a licence issued by the Central Bank of Myanmar
permitting the operation of a foreign remittance business.
(c) “Remittance business licence holder” means a person who has obtained a licence issued
by the Central Bank of Myanmar permitting the operation of a foreign remittance
business.
(d) “Bank with an authorised dealer licence (AD bank)” means a bank as defined in section
2 (j) Foreign Exchange Management Law.
(e) “Customer” means a sender or recipient who uses the services of a remittance business
licence holder.

(f) “Agent or branch office” means an agent or intermediary agent appointed abroad, or a

Chapter 2
Requirements for a licence application
4. An applicant for a remittance business licence must submit the following documents and evidence

Myanmar Companies Law;
(b) regarding the security deposit, evidence that the funds are obtained from legitimate
business activities and have been taxed;
(c) names, experience, and areas of expertise of the beneficial owner of the company, the
person who will manage the foreign remittance business, and the other managers;
evidence of their clean criminal record; and evidence of a clean criminal record of the
shareholders;
(d) name, experience, and evidence of a clean criminal record of the compliance officer who
will ensure compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering Law and the Counter-Terrorism
Law when the the foreign remittance business is operated;
(e) certificate that the compliance officer completed training to ensure compliance with the
provisions of the Anti-Money Laundering Law and the Counter-Terrorism Law, conducted
jointly by the Central Bank of Myanmar and law enforcement agencies such as the
Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), the Myanmar Police Force, and the Bureau of Special
Investigation;
(f) a statement that the foreign remittance business will be operated in cooperation with a
business that legally operates a foreign remittance business abroad, or through one’s own
branch office which is legally permitted to operate a foreign remittance business abroad;
(g) a business plan describing the methods to be used for employing information technology
(IT) or mobile technology;
(h) arrangements to link to domestic banks and mobile financial service businesses for
distributing and paying out money to recipients in various regions within Myanmar;

(i) if operating with an agent or branch office abroad, evidence of a clean criminal record of
such agent or branch office manager;
(j) evidence that the foreign company, agent, or branch office used for the foreign
remittance business already holds a licence to operate a foreign remittance business in
their respective country;
(k) a written undertaking that the applicant understands and will comply with the laws,
including the Foreign Exchange Management Law, the Financial Institutions Law, the Anti-
Money Laundering Law, and the Counter-Terrorism Law, as well as the rules, regulations,
disciplines, notifications, orders, directives, and procedures issued by financial regulatory
bodies including the Central Bank of Myanmar;
(l) a presentation or description of adequate arrangements for basic requirements such as
accurate record-keeping, counting received funds, and auditing;
(m) arrangements by the company regarding the receipt or remittance of funds from workers
employed abroad;
(n) arrangements for handling customer complaints.
5. The Central Bank of Myanmar shall decide to reject or approve the application within 90 days
from the date of receipt of the complete application, and shall notify the remittance business
licence applicant accordingly.

kyats is required due to the large scale of the business, the remittance business licence
holder shall comply with the direction of the Central Bank of Myanmar.

with the permission of the Central Bank of Myanmar. This fund shall be kept separately
from any other accounts (if any) of the remittance business licence holder and not

Allocation Law which are issued annually.

exist and operate after the expiry of its Registration Certificate.

organization endorsing that the objectives and activities to be implemented by the
association align with policies and goals, and can genuinely contribute to the
department's work, other than an implicit statement of support.

produced foods are safe and meet quality standards, and to make the application process for Food
Manufacturing Recommendations easier, faster, and smoother, aiming to develop a more robust
inspection system, supervision will be carried out in accordance with the procedures for applying for Food
Manufacturing Recommendations for domestic food businesses. Domestic food businesses are
scrutinized and processed according to the following procedures.

title: Matters to be scrutinsed when taking affidavits for marriages between foreigners and Myanmar women
text:

Republic of the Union of Myanmar
Supreme Court of the Union
Directive No. 1/2025
1387, 13th Waning Day of Tazaungmon
(17 November 2025)
Matters to be scrutinsed when taking affidavits for marriages between foreigners and Myanmar
women
1. Courts accept and take marriage affidavits that those marrying as Buddhists make on their own
volition. In this context, the Supreme Court of the Union has issued directives and exercises
supervision to ensure that the rights of Myanmar women wishing to marry foreigners are not lost.
2. It must be acknowledged that circumstances have changed and human trafficking, whereby
foreigners visit Myanmar to take young Myanmar women out of the country after deceiving and
marrying them under false pretenses, is on the rise. As more scrutiny is needed to prevent
fraudulent marriages by foreigners, courts are again directed, if there is an application to take
marriage affidavits, to take the affidavits as prescribed only after carefully scrutinising whether the
following particulars are complete.
For the foreigner intending to marry:
(1) Passport;
(2) evidence of a visa that allows the foreigner to stay in Myanmar for more than 30 days;
(3) submission to the Myanmar Immigration Department stating that the marriage will take
place during the stay with the visa;
(4) certificate from the relevant embassy stating that the marriage is not prohibited under
the law of the relevant country (“certificate of no impediment to marriage”), submitted
together with the following documents:
(a) certificates showing that the foreigner is a bachelor or not married anymore
(evidence of divorce or the spouse’s death), the foreigner’s permanent address
and occupation in the relevant country, the foreigner’s income, and that the
foreigner is of good character or has no criminal record, all to be submitted in a
relevant language (e.g., Burmese or English) and properly certified by a notary or
- 1 -
No. 55 (D), Inya Myaing Road, Bahan Township, Yangon Region
Phone: +95-9-262546284 (English) or +95-9-886699332 (Myanmar)
E-mail: info@lincolnmyanmar.com - Web: www.lincolnmyanmar.com

LINCOLN LEGAL SERVICES (MYANMAR) LIMITED
the relevant embassy; if the foreigner is self-employed, the business
certificate/license issued by the relevant authority must also be submitted;
(b) certificate from the relevant country stating whether Myanmar women or men
who marry a national of the other country are eligible for citizenship;
(c) certificate or law from the relevant country stating whether children born to the
parents mentioned in the above paragraph are eligible for citizenship.
3. Existing legal provisions, directives and orders concerning the taking of marriage affidavits shall
continue to apply alongside this directive.

1387, 6th Waning Day of Tazaungmon

The Ministry of Defence, exercising the authority vested under Section 23 (b) of the Military Secrets
Preservation and Protection Law, hereby issues the following directive to enable any former defence
personnel member to work as a private security employee as prescribed:
Chapter (1)
Name and Definitions
1. This directive shall be called the Directive on Applications by Former Defence Personnel Members
for Permission to Work as Private Security Employees.
2. The expressions contained in this directive shall have the meanings assigned to them in the
Military Secrets Preservation and Protection Law. Furthermore, the following expressions shall
have the meanings assigned hereunder:
(a) Law means the Military Secrets Preservation and Protection Law.
(b) Permission means the permission issued by the Ministry under this Law to work as a
private security employee.
(c) Applicant means any former defence personnel member applying to work as a private
security employee.
(d) Form means a form contained in this directive.
Chapter (2)
Application for Permission
3. Any former defence personnel member wishing to work as a private security employee must apply
for permission to the Ministry with Form (1), along with a cover letter from the relevant private
security services business and three copies of the following supporting documents:

(c) Original endorsement of having no criminal record from the relevant Township Police

(d) Three photographs for the license (1.5 × 1.75 inches, photographs must have been taken
within 1 month).
4. If any former defence personnel member was working as a private security employee before this
Law came into force, such person must apply for permission within six months from the date on
which this Law came into force.
5. If the permission granted is damaged or lost, the recipient must apply for a copy of the permission
to the Ministry with Form (2), along with the cover letter from the relevant private security
services business and three copies of the following supporting documents:
(a) Copy of the Citizenship Scrutiny Card;

personnel member;
(c) Original endorsement of having no criminal record from the relevant Township Police
Chief (the endorsement must have been obtained within 30 days);
(d) Copy of the previous permission, if any;
(e) Original undertaking confirming that the permission is damaged or lost;
(f) Three photographs for the license (1.5 × 1.75 inches, photographs must have been taken
within 1 month).
Chapter (3)
Verification, Granting or Refusal
6. The Ministry shall:
(a) verify whether Form (1) submitted by the applicant for permission and the attached supporting
documents comply with the provisions;

(c) forward Form (1) and the attached supporting documents to relevant departments and
organisations to verify their correctness;
(d) verify whether the applicant has ever been prosecuted for high treason, any offense
under the Counter-Terrorism Law, any offense under the Unlawful Associations Act, or
any offense designated by the Ministry as one for which permission should not be granted.
7. After verification in accordance with the provisions in Section 6, the Ministry shall, within 60 days
from the date of receipt of the application:
(a) if it decides to grant permission, issue the permission to the applicant in Form (4);
(b) if it decides to refuse permission, notify the applicant of the refusal.
Chapter (4)
Application for Renewal, Granting or Refusal
8. If the recipient of the permission wishes to continue working, they must apply with Form (3) to
the Ministry for renewal of the permission 60 days before the expiration of the permission, along
with a cover letter from the relevant private security services business and the original previous
permission.
9. The Ministry, after verifying the application submitted under Section 8:
(a) if it decides to grant renewal, shall collect the original previous permission and issue a
new permission to the applicant in Form (4) stating the period of renewal;
(b) if it decides to refuse, shall notify the applicant of the refusal to renew the permission.
10. If the application for renewal is not submitted within the stipulated period, the permission shall
be deemed to have become automatically void on the date of its expiration.
Chapter (5)
Duties to be Complied with by Permission Recipients and Private Security Services Businesses

11. Any former defence personnel member working as a private security employee has the duty to
comply with the following:
(a) uphold and respect the gratitude owed to the State and the organisation in which they
served;
(b) refrain from exerting undue influence or from connecting and dealing, for the benefit of
domestic or foreign organisations and companies, with the officers and personnel
currently serving in the organisations in which they had served;
(c) work only with the private security services business stated in the permission;
(d) if wishing to continue working, apply for renewal of permission within 60 days before the
expiration of the permission;
(e) if no longer wishing to work as a private security employee, return the permission.
12. If any of the following events occur regarding a permission recipient serving in its business, the
private security services business must promptly notify the Ministry:
(a) transfer to work at another private security services business;
(b) voluntary resignation;
(c) dismissal;
(d) being prosecuted for a criminal offence;
(e) death.
Chapter (6)
General
13. The term of permission is set as three years.
14. The Ministry may revoke the permission if the recipient fails to comply with any of the duties to
be complied with under Section 11 or fails to comply with any provision stipulated by the Ministry
from time to time.
15. If any private security services business fails to comply with any of the duties to be complied with
under Section 12, the Ministry shall notify the Private Security Services Supervisory Central
Committee so that necessary action can be taken against such business.
